lesson_title: The Spaza Shop Runs on the Same Accounting as a Supermarket
hook_text: Your aunty's spaza shop uses the same accounting as Checkers. She just never wrote it down.
clip_script: In her head: I took R4 500 this month. I spent about R3 000 at the wholesaler. So I made about R1 500. Sounds right. Now the notebook version, honestly, line by line. Sales in the tin: R4 500. Stock bought: R3 000. Taxi to the wholesaler, four trips at R40: R160. Electricity for the fridge: R90. Airtime used for orders: R50. Now the profit line: R1 200. The head said R1 500; the notebook says R1 200. Where did R300 go? Nowhere — it was always being spent. The head just couldn't hold the small amounts, so they leaked.
visual_style: Split screen: a thought bubble tallying big round numbers on one side, a notebook filling line by line on the other, with R300 in coins visibly slipping through fingers between them.
pacing: Conversational build through the numbers, beat of silence on the gap, gentle punchline.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — the shop on your street is the whole syllabus.
